sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If there's one thing we like here at 99PI, it's serendipity.
sentences.zh: 如果说我们在《99%隐形》节目里有什么特别推崇的东西，那就是“机缘巧合”。

sentences.en: Those little unexpected moments of magic that puncture the flaws of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 那些在日常生活的缝隙中，偶尔迸发出的意想不到的奇妙瞬间。

sentences.en: But why leave serendipity to chance?
sentences.zh: 但为什么要让这种机缘巧合听天由命呢？

sentences.en: What if you could design serendipity into someone's life
sentences.zh: 如果能把这种机缘巧合，或者其他某种奇妙的体验设计进别人的生活中，

sentences.en: or some other magical experience to make a better world?
sentences.zh: 从而让世界变得更美好，那会怎样呢？

sentences.en: Well, our friends at Death, Sex, and Money found someone who does just that.
sentences.zh: 我们的朋友在《死亡、性与金钱》节目里，就找到了这样一位能做到这一点的人。

sentences.en: He calls himself an experienced designer, but that title might undersell him a little bit.
sentences.zh: 他自称是“体验设计师”，但这个头衔可能还有点低估他了。

sentences.en: To quote the great Tony Hawk,
sentences.zh: 引用伟大的托尼·霍克的话来说：

sentences.en: He's f***ing Willy Wonka.
sentences.zh: 他简直就是个该死的威利·旺卡。

sentences.en: And the equally great Anna Sale at Death, Sex, and Money would like to introduce him to you.
sentences.zh: 同样伟大的《死亡、性与金钱》主持人安娜·塞尔，想把他介绍给你们认识。

sentences.en: Skateboarding legend Tony Hawk hosted a podcast with radio personality Jason Ellis.
sentences.zh: 滑板传奇人物托尼·霍克曾与电台名人杰森·埃利斯共同主持过一档播客。

sentences.en: Hey everybody, it's Jason Ellis and Tony Hawk.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是杰森·埃利斯和托尼·霍克。

sentences.en: Hawk vs. Wolf, greatest podcast of all time in the history of the universe.
sentences.zh: 《霍克对决狼》，宇宙历史上最伟大的播客。

sentences.en: What he said about our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么评价我们的播客的。

sentences.en: On an episode last year, Jason asked about a recent trip Tony had been on.
sentences.zh: 在去年的一期节目中，杰森问起了托尼最近的一次旅行。

sentences.en: You were in the desert.
sentences.zh: 你当时在沙漠里。

sentences.en: Okay, I'll explain it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来解释一下。

sentences.en: Let me take it from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 让我从头说起。

sentences.en: There's a guy I know that I've become friends with in New York,
sentences.zh: 我在纽约认识了一个朋友，

sentences.en: and he creates experiences.
sentences.zh: 他专门创造各种体验。

sentences.en: And when I say creates experiences, I cannot do it justice of what he is capable of
sentences.zh: 当我提到“创造体验”时，我真的无法用言语来形容他的能力，

sentences.en: and what he has put together for people.
sentences.zh: 以及他为人们策划出的那些东西。

sentences.en: The guy who helped Tony is named Indy Austin.
sentences.zh: 帮助托尼的那个人叫印第·奥斯汀。

sentences.en: But if you're thinking high-end party host or wedding planner for rich people and celebrities,
sentences.zh: 但如果你以为他只是那种为富人和名人服务的高端派对策划人或婚礼策划师，

sentences.en: you've got the wrong idea.
sentences.zh: 那你就大错特错了。

sentences.en: I went to his place in New York.
sentences.zh: 我去过他在纽约的住处。

sentences.en: The last time I visited, we were just talking about other stuff.
sentences.zh: 上次拜访时，我们只是在聊些别的事情。

sentences.en: And I said, would you consider doing something from my office?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，你有没有考虑过为我的办公室策划点什么？

sentences.en: Because we have a holiday thing every year, but I'm kind of running out of ideas.
sentences.zh: 因为我们每年都有节日活动，但我实在想不出什么新花样了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: He's just like, what can we work with?
sentences.zh: 他只是问，我们能利用什么资源？

sentences.en: And I said, well, I'd like to do something that is relatively close,
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，我希望能做一些距离相对近一点的事情，

sentences.en: but if we have to drive a little bit, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 但如果需要开车走一段路，也没问题。

sentences.en: And those are the only parameters I gave him.
sentences.zh: 这就是我给他的全部要求。

sentences.en: I don't know what he's planning, right?
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道他在策划什么，对吧？

sentences.en: And so we have our weekly meeting, and everyone's there.
sentences.zh: 后来我们开周会时，大家都在场。

sentences.en: And then there were all these gifts on the desk, which was not the usual holiday gift exchange.
sentences.zh: 桌上突然多了很多礼物，这可不是平时的节日礼物交换环节。

sentences.en: And so I get instructions, like, open the gifts.
sentences.zh: 然后我收到了指令，比如，打开这些礼物。

sentences.en: So we open the gifts.
sentences.zh: 于是我们打开了礼物。

sentences.en: There's like a shovel, a pickaxe, a first aid kit.
sentences.zh: 里面有铲子、鹤嘴锄、急救箱之类的东西。

sentences.en: There's a locked briefcase and a set of keys.
sentences.zh: 还有一个锁着的公文包和一串钥匙。

sentences.en: We look outside, and there's this passenger van.
sentences.zh: 我们往外一看，停着一辆客货两用车。

sentences.en: And then I just get a location.
sentences.zh: 接着我只收到一个地点信息。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We just start driving out to the desert, and we are driving.
sentences.zh: 我们就这样开车驶向沙漠，一直在开。

sentences.en: I mean, signs are like, no motorized vehicles past this point, government property.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，路标上写着“此处禁止机动车辆通行，政府财产”。

sentences.en: And then we go around this corner, and there's a train.
sentences.zh: 然后我们转过一个弯，看到了一列火车。

sentences.en: Indy and his team built a five-car train from old parts.
sentences.zh: 印第和他的团队用旧零件拼凑出了一列五节车厢的火车。

sentences.en: It ran on abandoned tracks on public land in a Southern California desert.
sentences.zh: 它在南加州沙漠公共土地上的一条废弃铁轨上运行。

sentences.en: It was whimsical, a piano player on one car, a bar car.
sentences.zh: 这太奇思妙想了，一节车厢里有钢琴师，还有一节酒吧车厢。

sentences.en: But at the center of the experience was a ceremony.
sentences.zh: 但整个体验的核心是一个仪式。

sentences.en: Like most of the things Indy designs, at some point you encounter a personal challenge that cuts you to the quick.
sentences.zh: 就像印第设计的多数事物一样，在某个时刻，你会遇到一个直击你心灵深处的个人挑战。

sentences.en: Tony said there were some relationships among his colleagues that needed mending.
sentences.zh: 托尼说，他同事之间有些关系需要修复。

sentences.en: When the train was far out, Indy gave the team a bottle of whiskey and told them to bury it and make a promise.
sentences.zh: 当火车开到荒野深处时，印第给了团队一瓶威士忌，让他们埋下它并许下承诺。

sentences.en: We go bury this bottle that we made a pact about.
sentences.zh: 我们去埋下了那瓶酒，并立下了誓言。

sentences.en: If one of us passes away, we're going to go find the bottle and share it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们其中一人去世了，我们就要去找到那瓶酒并一起分享。

sentences.en: In this episode, I talked to Tony Hawk and the train builder, Indy Austin, who has designed hundreds of experiences,
sentences.zh: 在这一集中，我采访了托尼·霍克和火车建造者印第·奥斯汀，他设计过数百种体验，

sentences.en: from scavenger hunts to coming-of-age rituals and funerals.
sentences.zh: 从寻宝游戏到成年礼，再到葬礼，应有尽有。

sentences.en: And for me, talking to Indy about the origins of his work and the meaning behind it all was transformative.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，与印第探讨他工作的起源以及背后的意义，是一次脱胎换骨的经历。

sentences.en: Prepare to be wowed.
sentences.zh: 准备好被震撼吧。

sentences.en: My job as a designer of experiences is just to place stepping stones.
sentences.zh: 作为一名体验设计师，我的工作就是放置垫脚石。

sentences.en: So I'm creating a whole scenario of some type, but it's just a series of stepping stones.
sentences.zh: 我创造的是某种完整的场景，但它只是一系列垫脚石。

sentences.en: Story results out of that, but it isn't a story I'm telling.
sentences.zh: 故事由此而生，但这并不是我在讲述一个故事。

sentences.en: It's something that happens personal to you.
sentences.zh: 这是发生在你个人身上的事情。

sentences.en: This is Death, Sex, and Money.
sentences.zh: 这里是《死亡、性与金钱》。

sentences.en: The show from Slate, about the things we think about a lot.
sentences.zh: 这是Slate出品的节目，关于那些我们经常思考的事情。

sentences.en: We need to talk about more.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多地谈论这些。

sentences.en: I'm Anna Sale.
sentences.zh: 我是安娜·塞尔。

sentences.en: Tony Hawk first bonded with Indy Austin over their love of rare whiskeys.
sentences.zh: 托尼·霍克最初是因为对稀有威士忌的共同爱好而与印第·奥斯汀结缘的。

sentences.en: Before Indy designed an experience for Tony, he hosted Tony and his wife at his tiny bar, which seats two guests.
sentences.zh: 在印第为托尼设计体验之前，他曾在自己那间只能容纳两名客人的小酒吧里招待过托尼和他的妻子。

sentences.en: It's made to look like a toll booth you'd find on the highway.
sentences.zh: 它被设计成看起来像高速公路上的收费站。

sentences.en: So he's at the toll booth side of it, and then you're where the window would be, but the window's behind you.
sentences.zh: 他站在收费站的一侧，而你站在窗口的位置，但窗口其实在你身后。

sentences.en: And he has this whole selection of bottles and stuff behind him.
sentences.zh: 他身后摆满了各种各样的酒瓶。

sentences.en: But it's, I mean, it's tight.
sentences.zh: 但空间非常狭窄。

sentences.en: Like, the three, yes, there are three people in it, but there's no room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，里面确实能挤进三个人，但再也放不下任何东西了。

sentences.en: And I imagine in your work and in your life, you've been around a lot of people who do things a little differently.
sentences.zh: 我想在你的工作和生活中，你一定接触过很多行事风格与众不同的人。

sentences.en: Like, what is it, when you think of him and what he's able to dream up, do you think that, like, what is it that he allows himself to do that other people just don't?
sentences.zh: 当你想到他以及他所能构思出的那些东西时，你觉得他允许自己去做而别人却做不到的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Like, what makes what he does special?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他的工作如此特别？

sentences.en: I think he works outside the limits, well, firstly, of the law and of any sort of limitations of what you think, where you think you can go,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是在界限之外工作，首先是法律的界限，以及你对“你能去哪里”的任何限制，

sentences.en: what you think you can be involved with.
sentences.zh: 或者你认为自己能参与什么事情的限制。

sentences.en: I think it's more of that element, that he sees a landscape or a city, and he sees it for possibilities and opportunities to, you know, oh, what if we could get up there?
sentences.zh: 我觉得更多是因为他看待风景或城市的方式，他看到的是各种可能性和机会，比如，“噢，如果我们能爬到那上面去会怎样？”

sentences.en: It kind of reminds me of, like, how I think of skaters, like, you know, scanning the landscape for where they can skate.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起滑板手们思考的方式，你知道，他们会扫描周围环境，寻找可以滑板的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, you see the world in a totally different perspective.
sentences.zh: 没错，你以一种完全不同的视角看待世界。

sentences.en: Seeing things from a different perspective, for skaters and for Indy, sometimes involves trespassing.
sentences.zh: 对于滑板手和印第来说，从不同的视角看事物，有时意味着擅闯禁地。

sentences.en: Indy has been known to create speakeasies in water towers, hotel basements, and once for Tony Hawk in the San Diego sewer system.
sentences.zh: 印第曾因在水塔、酒店地下室，甚至有一次为托尼·霍克在圣地亚哥的下水道系统中创建地下酒吧而闻名。

sentences.en: And then we go down, and there's this entire passageway under the street that I don't know existed.
sentences.zh: 然后我们走下去，街道下面竟然有整整一条我根本不知道存在的通道。

sentences.en: And then we walk below San Diego for a couple miles.
sentences.zh: 我们就这样在圣地亚哥地下走了几英里。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So we're in, like, we're the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就像是《忍者神龟》一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, the fact that I, sure, I facilitated it in the sense that I paid for it, but also, you know, that I tapped his resources and his imagination.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，虽然我确实在某种意义上促成了这件事，因为我付了钱，但我也利用了他的资源和想象力。

sentences.en: He's fucking Willy Wonka.
sentences.zh: 他就是个该死的威利·旺卡。

sentences.en: Like Willy Wonka, the experience's Indy designs can be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 就像威利·旺卡一样，印第设计的体验有时可能很危险。

sentences.en: Like once he helped a wife of a well-known author recreate a kidnapping scene from one of the author's books.
sentences.zh: 比如有一次，他帮助一位知名作家的妻子重现了该作家书中描述的绑架场景。

sentences.en: They also can reveal something about your character.
sentences.zh: 这些体验也能揭示你性格中的某些东西。

sentences.en: According to Tony Hawk, Indy helped a high-profile couple after infidelity.
sentences.zh: 据托尼·霍克说，印第曾帮助一对在出轨风波后的知名夫妇。

sentences.en: Some big, uh, hip-hop artist, I'm not sure who or what the, who it was at all, created this whole experience because he wanted to apologize or make up to...
sentences.zh: 某个大牌嘻哈歌手，我完全不确定是谁，策划了整个体验，因为他想道歉或弥补……

sentences.en: Indy did not want to talk about this job.
sentences.zh: 印第不想谈论这份工作。

sentences.en: And at every turn, she had to make a choice.
sentences.zh: 在每一个转折点，她都必须做出选择。

sentences.en: And Indy also designs rituals for things we all go through, like a coming-of-age ceremony for a 13-year-old boy.
sentences.zh: 印第还为我们都会经历的事情设计仪式，比如为一名13岁男孩设计的成年礼。

sentences.en: They stranded him alone on an abandoned island with a backpack, food, and a flare.
sentences.zh: 他们把他独自留在了一座荒岛上，只带了一个背包、食物和信号弹。

sentences.en: And he designs funerals.
sentences.zh: 他还设计葬礼。

sentences.en: That's really where it all started.
sentences.zh: 那真的是一切的起点。

sentences.en: I met Indy Austin in our Slate offices in New York City back in June.
sentences.zh: 今年六月，我在纽约的Slate办公室见到了印第·奥斯汀。

sentences.en: It doesn't take that long to learn he is obsessed with locks and keys and scan spaces that could be used for experiences.
sentences.zh: 不用多久你就会发现，他痴迷于锁具、钥匙以及那些可以用于体验的空间。

sentences.en: Like when we gave him the key card to give him access to the bathroom, he took his time to see where else in the building it would work.
sentences.zh: 比如当我们给他门禁卡让他进入洗手间时，他花时间去查看这卡在楼里其他地方还能不能用。

sentences.en: When he came back, he said sneakily, this opens so many doors.
sentences.zh: 他回来时鬼鬼祟祟地说：“这玩意儿能打开好多门。”

sentences.en: When we sat down to talk for the interview, he presented me with a present, a little metal thing that was about the size of a credit card, with different grooves cut out.
sentences.zh: 当我们坐下来准备采访时，他送了我一份礼物，一个大约信用卡大小的金属片，上面刻着不同的凹槽。

sentences.en: He had to explain to me I could use this to pick all kinds of locks.
sentences.zh: 他向我解释说，我可以用这个来撬开各种锁。

sentences.en: I brought this to give to you in a way to show you that I'm giving you permission to unlock something.
sentences.zh: 我带这个来送给你，是想告诉你，我允许你去解锁某些东西。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 噢，好吧。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 噢，好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Or, well, if we're going to unpack.
sentences.zh: 或者说，如果我们打算深入探讨的话。

sentences.en: I thought you were just letting me break my rules.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你只是在让我打破规则呢。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, that's great.
sentences.zh: 噢，那太棒了。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: I don't want to tell you that in advance, that that's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 我不想提前告诉你，不想让你知道正在发生什么。

sentences.en: That's just how I – that's where that is coming from in me.
sentences.zh: 这就是我——这就是我内心深处的想法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And this is exactly how I – this is a great example of how I work, which is I won't normally tell you what I think it means to me.
sentences.zh: 这正是我工作方式的一个绝佳例子，通常我不会告诉你我认为它对我意味着什么。

sentences.en: I'll let you have your own experience of it.
sentences.zh: 我会让你自己去体验它。

sentences.en: But to me, I'm thinking, okay, if I'm going to talk to someone I don't know and let them ask me a bunch of questions I don't know, how am I approaching that?
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，我在想，如果我要和一个我不认识的人交谈，让他们问我一堆我不知道的问题，我该如何应对？

sentences.en: And my approach is, I'm going to see if we can unlock something.
sentences.zh: 我的方法是，看看我们能否解锁点什么。

sentences.en: I don't – or, you know, we're going to get in.
sentences.zh: 我不知道——或者说，我们要进入某种状态。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: But maybe there's somewhere we go.
sentences.zh: 但也许我们能去某个地方。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: It makes people ask, what is that?
sentences.zh: 这让人不禁问，那是什么？

sentences.en: It almost sounds like a tech job.
sentences.zh: 听起来几乎像是一份科技工作。

sentences.en: It sounds like a user experience job.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是一份用户体验设计工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good smokescreen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是个很好的掩护。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: There's no formalized field that is experience design for real world in-person things.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有一个正式的领域是专门针对现实世界面对面体验设计的。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So we don't have a convenient container for it yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还没有一个方便的词汇来定义它。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有趣吗？

sentences.en: Like, we have a word for performance art.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们有“行为艺术”这个词。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if there's, like, something artificial, an artifice happening in real life, we have that word.
sentences.zh: 所以如果现实生活中发生了某种人为的、虚构的事情，我们有那个词。

sentences.en: If it's an event, we have an event designer or event planner.
sentences.zh: 如果是活动，我们有活动设计师或活动策划人。

sentences.en: But experience is different because it's – well, how is an experience different from an event?
sentences.zh: 但“体验”是不同的，因为——那么，体验和活动有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: So one way of saying it, you could say that, like, every event is something that you can experience if you're being present for it.
sentences.zh: 一种说法是，你可以说如果你身临其境，那么每一个活动都是你可以体验的东西。

sentences.en: But a thing that I'm always trying to make is something that isn't just an occurrence out there in the world,
sentences.zh: 但我一直试图创造的东西，不仅仅是世界上发生的一个事件，

sentences.en: but is an occurrence inside you in a way that matters to you personally.
sentences.zh: 而是发生在你内心深处，对你个人而言意义重大的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The first thing I want to know about, of all of the different things that you have designed, can you tell me about designing experiences around funeral rituals?
sentences.zh: 我想了解的第一件事是，在你设计过的各种事物中，你能跟我讲讲关于为葬礼仪式设计体验的事吗？

sentences.en: Like, how did you first work on some kind of ritual for celebrating the life of somebody after they were gone?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是如何第一次着手为某人身后事设计某种纪念仪式的？

sentences.en: So I grew up near a town in southeast Alaska where – a little village out in the islands that had very powerful funeral traditions.
sentences.zh: 我是在阿拉斯加东南部的一个小镇附近长大的，那是一个位于岛屿上的小村庄，有着非常隆重的葬礼传统。

sentences.en: My parents are – my mother's playing the piano and my father's playing the cello and I'm singing.
sentences.zh: 我的父母——我母亲弹钢琴，我父亲拉大提琴，而我在唱歌。

sentences.en: And these funerals would go on for many, many hours.
sentences.zh: 这些葬礼通常会持续很多很多个小时。

sentences.en: It would be really long.
sentences.zh: 时间非常长。

sentences.en: So long that a meal would be served in the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 长到中间还会供应一顿饭。

sentences.en: People would be taking naps.
sentences.zh: 人们会小睡一会儿。

sentences.en: Then there would be dancing.
sentences.zh: 然后会有舞蹈。

sentences.en: Then there would be more music.
sentences.zh: 接着会有更多的音乐。

sentences.en: Then there would be really long speeches.
sentences.zh: 然后会有非常冗长的演讲。

sentences.en: Then there'd be even more speeches.
sentences.zh: 接着还会有更多的演讲。

sentences.en: Then speeches would come after the speeches.
sentences.zh: 演讲之后还有演讲。

sentences.en: And then there'd be more music.
sentences.zh: 然后又会有更多的音乐。

sentences.en: And, like, we might sing several times throughout this and then just be, like, hanging out in this, you know, giant funeral tradition.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们可能会在整个过程中唱好几次歌，然后就只是待在那儿，沉浸在这种，你知道的，宏大的葬礼传统之中。

sentences.en: How should I understand, like, the faith tradition that these funerals were a part of?
sentences.zh: 我该如何理解这些葬礼所从属的信仰传统呢？

sentences.en: That village that I grew up near is a Tlingit native village.
sentences.zh: 我长大的那个村庄是一个特林吉特原住民村庄。

sentences.en: That's – the tribe is Tlingit.
sentences.zh: 那是——那个部落是特林吉特族。

sentences.en: And it is probably about 80% native, maybe.
sentences.zh: 大概有80%是原住民吧，可能。

sentences.en: Is your family indigenous?
sentences.zh: 你的家庭是原住民吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不是，不是。

sentences.en: My family is a classic American Catholic combination of Irish and Italian.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭是典型的美国天主教家庭，由爱尔兰和意大利血统组成。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: In the 70s, my parents decided they wanted to move out to the woods, which was a thing that was happening a lot at that time.
sentences.zh: 在70年代，我父母决定搬到森林里去住，这在当时是很流行的一种做法。

sentences.en: Kind of like a back-to-the-land tradition, like hippie sort of infused vibe in your family?
sentences.zh: 有点像那种回归土地的传统，你家里有一种嬉皮士式的氛围？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is the community you grew up in?
sentences.zh: 这就是你成长的社区吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How many people?
sentences.zh: 有多少人？

sentences.en: Usually about 60, 70 people, something like that.
sentences.zh: 通常大约60、70人左右，差不多那样。

sentences.en: Small.
sentences.zh: 很小。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How many kids were around?
sentences.zh: 周围有多少孩子？

sentences.en: Not many.
sentences.zh: 不多。

sentences.en: Most of the time.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候是这样。

sentences.en: A lot of the time when I was a kid, it was just me and a lot of adults.
sentences.zh: 我小时候大部分时间里，周围就只有我和一群成年人。

sentences.en: So this is a huge part of your life because then if there's a lot of older people in the community – I mean, there were – funerals were part of what happened in life.
sentences.zh: 所以这对你的生活影响巨大，因为如果社区里有很多长者——我是说，确实有——葬礼就是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: You showed up.
sentences.zh: 你会出席。

sentences.en: You were a part of this ceremony.
sentences.zh: 你是这个仪式的一部分。

sentences.en: You had a role to play, but other people played other roles.
sentences.zh: 你有自己的角色要扮演，而其他人则扮演其他角色。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think about it, there's more funerals than there are weddings.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你仔细想想，葬礼其实比婚礼还要多。

sentences.en: But actually, let me tell you – let me skip ahead to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 但其实，让我告诉你——让我跳到成年之后的事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't know I was going to, like – I don't know, that funerals would continue to be important.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不知道我会——我不知道，我没想到葬礼会一直如此重要。

sentences.en: I mean, it's amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这很神奇。

sentences.en: Everyone we know dies at some point and or you do firSt.
sentences.zh: 我们认识的每个人最终都会死去，或者你先走一步。

sentences.en: So funerals are a really important part of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以葬礼是你生活中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: But, like, do you spend a lot of time thinking about, like, all the funerals you're going to attend of all the people you love?
sentences.zh: 但是，你会花很多时间去思考，比如，你将来要参加所有你所爱之人的葬礼吗？

sentences.en: You want to spend time thinking about, like, all the fun stuff you're going to do together.
sentences.zh: 你更想花时间去思考你们在一起要做的那些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: So I went to a funeral that was for a friend of mine who died young.
sentences.zh: 所以我去参加了一位英年早逝的朋友的葬礼。

sentences.en: And his mother was kind of running the funeral.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲在主持葬礼。

sentences.en: And I think in her grief, what made sense to her was to have this funeral be all about Jesus.
sentences.zh: 我想在她的悲痛中，她觉得最合理的方式就是让这场葬礼完全围绕耶稣展开。

sentences.en: It was a super Jesus-centric funeral, which maybe makes sense if Jesus is your thing.
sentences.zh: 那是一场极其以耶稣为中心的葬礼，如果耶稣是你的信仰，这或许说得通。

sentences.en: It's what made sense to his mother.
sentences.zh: 这对他的母亲来说是合理的。

sentences.en: But as his friend, sitting in the audience, I remember being horrified at how this didn't actually honor him.
sentences.zh: 但作为他的朋友，坐在观众席上，我记得我当时感到非常震惊，因为这根本没有真正纪念他。

sentences.en: He was, like, a, you know, avowed atheiSt.
sentences.zh: 他可是个，你知道的，公开的无神论者。

sentences.en: And he would have been horrified if he'd seen what we were saying in his name.
sentences.zh: 如果他看到我们以他的名义所说的一切，他会感到震惊的。

sentences.en: And I didn't blame his mother.
sentences.zh: 我并不责怪他的母亲。

sentences.en: It made sense where she was coming from.
sentences.zh: 从她的立场来看，这很合理。

sentences.en: But I just remember thinking, oh, my God, this is such a missed opportunity to actually honor who this person actually was and who he was for who he was.
sentences.zh: 但我只记得当时心想，天哪，这真是错失了一个良机，没能真正去纪念这个人的本真，以及他之所以为他的原因。

sentences.en: The first funeral Indy ever designed came a few months after his friends.
sentences.zh: Indy设计的第一个葬礼是在他朋友去世几个月后进行的。

sentences.en: He got a letter from a woman who was dying, and she wanted help to plan her funeral.
sentences.zh: 他收到了一位垂死女性的来信，她想寻求帮助来规划自己的葬礼。

sentences.en: After talking, they decided that she would like to throw a big party after she was gone.
sentences.zh: 交谈之后，他们决定她希望在自己离世后举办一场盛大的派对。

sentences.en: It was simple and special.
sentences.zh: 那场葬礼既简单又特别。

sentences.en: Over the years, Indy's funeral planning has gotten more elaborate, like the one for a lawyer in New York City who had brain cancer.
sentences.zh: 多年来，Indy的葬礼策划变得越来越复杂，比如为一位患有脑癌的纽约律师设计的葬礼。

sentences.en: This man wrote me, and he said, I don't have any family members.
sentences.zh: 这个人写信给我，他说，我没有任何家人。

sentences.en: I have, like, one cousin somewhere who's been—everyone else in my family is gone.
sentences.zh: 我只有一个不知在哪里的表亲——我家里其他人都去世了。

sentences.en: I have no immediate family.
sentences.zh: 我没有直系亲属。

sentences.en: But I have a board game group, and it's five of my buddies, and we've been playing board games ever since we were in college.
sentences.zh: 但我有一个桌游小组，那是我的五个好哥们，我们从大学起就一直在一起玩桌游。

sentences.en: And he said, the first weekend freshman year, in our freshman year dorm in college, we all met and started playing board games.
sentences.zh: 他说，大一的第一个周末，在大学宿舍里，我们相遇并开始玩桌游。

sentences.en: And we've been meeting now every year since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我们每年都会聚会。

sentences.en: And we spend one weekend of the year, and we all get together.
sentences.zh: 我们每年会花一个周末聚在一起。

sentences.en: At this point, they're all scattered around, but they get together and play board games.
sentences.zh: 现在他们都散落在各地，但他们还是会聚在一起玩桌游。

sentences.en: And he said, I'm going to be the first one to die, and those guys are going to miss me.
sentences.zh: 他说，我将是第一个去世的人，那些家伙会想念我的。

sentences.en: But they're not going to want to, like, go to the cemetery with a shovel of dirt, and I don't know, you know, or whatever that is.
sentences.zh: 但他们肯定不想拿着铲子去墓地铲土，我不知道，或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: He was like, so the normal stuff doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 他说，所以常规的那一套根本说不通。

sentences.en: Can you make something?
sentences.zh: 你能做点什么吗？

sentences.en: I was like, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我说，当然可以。

sentences.en: We can absolutely make something.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对能做点什么。

sentences.en: We lived maybe another six months, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我们又过了大约六个月。

sentences.en: And the next, at the next board game night, after he died, the five friends gathered.
sentences.zh: 在他去世后的下一次桌游之夜，那五个朋友聚在了一起。

sentences.en: It was here, that was also here in New York.
sentences.zh: 就在这儿，也是在纽约。

sentences.en: And a messenger came to the door with a box.
sentences.zh: 一个快递员带着一个盒子来到了门口。

sentences.en: And they opened the box, and inside there was a game.
sentences.zh: 他们打开盒子，里面是一个游戏。

sentences.en: It was a board game.
sentences.zh: 那是一个桌游。

sentences.en: I would say it kind of looked like, it sort of looked like a Monopoly board, in that it was square.
sentences.zh: 我会说它看起来有点像，看起来有点像大富翁棋盘，因为它是个正方形的。

sentences.en: You unfold this cardboard thing, and it's square, and there's spaces around the outside, and you have little pieces and some dice and their cards.
sentences.zh: 你展开这个纸板，它是正方形的，外围有格子，还有小棋子、骰子和卡片。

sentences.en: And sort of, if you're picturing the face of a Monopoly board, it's kind of what it looked like.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下大富翁棋盘的样子，它看起来差不多就是那样。

sentences.en: But as they started to play, it became the game mechanisms of every board game that they had played together over the years.
sentences.zh: 但当他们开始玩的时候，它变成了他们多年来一起玩过的所有桌游的游戏机制。

sentences.en: A little piece taken from every different board game.
sentences.zh: 从每一个不同的桌游中提取的一小部分。

sentences.en: And as they drew cards, it became stories of their time together.
sentences.zh: 当他们抽卡时，卡片变成了他们在一起度过时光的故事。

sentences.en: And as they went around the board, they went backwards through time, and backwards through all the games that they'd played over the years.
sentences.zh: 当他们在棋盘上移动时，他们是在时光倒流，回顾他们多年来玩过的所有游戏。

sentences.en: All the way back until, by the end of the board, they were back in their freshman year dorm, meeting each other for the first time on that first night.
sentences.zh: 一直回到最后，当棋盘走完时，他们回到了大一的宿舍，回到了那个第一晚初次相遇的时刻。

sentences.en: And when they were done playing the game, the end state of the game was the final instructions were fold up the board and put it back in the box.
sentences.zh: 当他们玩完游戏时，游戏的最终状态和最后指令是把棋盘折叠起来放回盒子里。

sentences.en: And there was a secret compartment in the bottom of this big wooden box.
sentences.zh: 在这个大木盒的底部有一个暗格。

sentences.en: And in the secret compartment, there were his ashes and a collapsible shovel.
sentences.zh: 在暗格里，装着他的骨灰和一把可折叠的铲子。

sentences.en: And his final wish was that they take the box into Central Park in the middle of the night and dig a hole under this particular tree and bury the box,
sentences.zh: 他最后的愿望是让他们在半夜把盒子带到中央公园，在那棵特定的树下挖个洞，把盒子埋了，

sentences.en: which you're absolutely not supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 而这是绝对不被允许做的事情。

sentences.en: And that's what they did.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是那样做了。

sentences.en: The whole box that included the board game?
sentences.zh: 整个盒子，包括那个桌游？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They played the game one time, and then it was buried with him.
sentences.zh: 他们玩了一次游戏，然后它就和他一起被埋葬了。

sentences.en: Do you feel comfortable sharing what the process was of making that with him?
sentences.zh: 你愿意分享一下和他一起制作这个过程的感受吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Like how you sat with him, you gathered the stories, you thought about the mechanisms of the different games with him.
sentences.zh: 比如你是如何和他坐在一起，收集故事，并和他一起思考不同游戏的机制的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He was in pretty good shape.
sentences.zh: 他当时的状态还不错。

sentences.en: And so as soon as we came back to him and I said, I think the thing is a game.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们回到他身边，我说，我觉得这个东西应该是个游戏。

sentences.en: Like, what is your funeral?
sentences.zh: 比如，你的葬礼是什么？

sentences.en: Obviously, it's a game.
sentences.zh: 显然，它是一个游戏。

sentences.en: So what is this board game?
sentences.zh: 那么这个桌游是什么样的？

sentences.en: And it was his idea that it was all the games that they'd played.
sentences.zh: 他提议说，这应该是他们玩过的所有游戏。

sentences.en: And so we took game mechanic.
sentences.zh: 于是我们采用了游戏机制。

sentences.en: He made a huge list of all these games, and we kind of placed them by year.
sentences.zh: 他列了一份巨大的清单，列出了所有这些游戏，我们按年份把它们排好。

sentences.en: He was like, okay, well, this game came out in this year, and we tried it for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，这个游戏是这一年出的，我们第一次尝试玩它。

sentences.en: We hated it.
sentences.zh: 我们讨厌它。

sentences.en: And here's why we hated that game.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们讨厌那个游戏的原因。

sentences.en: It was terrible.
sentences.zh: 太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I was like, great, we can use that.
sentences.zh: 我说，太棒了，我们可以用那个。

sentences.en: We're going to use that piece.
sentences.zh: 我们要用那个部分。

sentences.en: Or this other game, we keep replaying this one over the years because actually it's really good.
sentences.zh: 或者另一个游戏，我们多年来一直反复玩，因为实际上它真的很棒。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's take some of the mechanisms of that.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们提取它的一些机制吧。

sentences.en: We ended up with a thing that was so complicated.
sentences.zh: 最终我们做出来的东西非常复杂。

sentences.en: There's no way I could ever play it or you could play it.
sentences.zh: 我或者你根本不可能玩得转。

sentences.en: You had to be the people.
sentences.zh: 你必须是那些人。

sentences.en: These game dudes.
sentences.zh: 这些游戏发烧友。

sentences.en: Yeah, you had to be these board game, you know, like mega board game nerds who really knew all the intricacies.
sentences.zh: 是的，你必须是那种桌游，你知道的，那种真正了解所有复杂细节的超级桌游极客。

sentences.en: Or who could remember and be like, oh, that game we played back in 2004.
sentences.zh: 或者那种能回忆起来说，哦，那是我们2004年玩的游戏。

sentences.en: That was a terrible game, and here's why it sucked.
sentences.zh: 那是个烂游戏，这就是它为什么烂的原因。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, we're going to use that.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了，我们要用那个。

sentences.en: You know, that's a good example of it being particular and peculiar for them because also, like, I wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个很好的例子，说明了它对他们来说是多么独特和奇特，因为我也没在现场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I only know about how it went.
sentences.zh: 我只知道后来发生的事。

sentences.en: You sent it via messenger.
sentences.zh: 你是通过快递员寄过去的。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: You never met.
sentences.zh: 你们从未见面。

sentences.en: No one else is there.
sentences.zh: 没有其他人在场。

sentences.en: You didn't get to witness them playing the game.
sentences.zh: 你没能亲眼看到他们玩这个游戏。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It wasn't for me.
sentences.zh: 这不是为我准备的。

sentences.en: It wasn't for anyone else.
sentences.zh: 也不是为其他人准备的。

sentences.en: That's a good example of, like, sometimes you're making a thing and you aren't supposed to be present for it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子，说明有时候你在制作某样东西时，并不需要出现在现场。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I don't need to be there.
sentences.zh: 我不需要在那儿。

sentences.en: Like, it's for the people it's for.
sentences.zh: 它是为那些特定的人准备的。

sentences.en: Maybe that sometimes includes me, but a lot of times it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 也许有时候包括我，但很多时候并不包括。

sentences.en: I want to go back now.
sentences.zh: 我现在想回到过去。

sentences.en: I want to be able to understand a little bit more of the through line of, so you're a child in a very small rural community in southeastern Alaska.
sentences.zh: 我想多了解一点其中的脉络，比如你作为一个在阿拉斯加东南部偏远小社区长大的孩子。

sentences.en: Did you have the sense as a child that you weren't going to stay there when you grew up?
sentences.zh: 你小时候有没有一种感觉，觉得长大后不会一直待在那里？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Did you, in your 20s, did you find yourself sort of gravitating to different systems to try them out?

sentences.zh: 比如教会或者……

sentences.en: I mean, I briefly, I would occasionally eyeball other systems briefly.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我偶尔会短暂地审视一下其他体系。

sentences.en: But very briefly, I wasn't like, I'm now lost without that system and have to get found or get saved or have some whole structure.
sentences.zh: 但非常短暂，我并没有那种“没有那个体系我就迷失了，必须得救或拥有某种完整结构”的感觉。

sentences.en: I was like, I'm just going to move without the structure and find out what happens.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我就要在没有结构的情况下前行，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Because I was curious about that.
sentences.zh: 因为我对此很好奇。

sentences.en: I was like, am I just immediately going to start murdering and raping people without a system?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，如果没有体系，我会不会立刻开始杀人放火？

sentences.en: What's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 会发生什么？

sentences.en: Am I...
sentences.zh: 我会……

sentences.en: Is that...
sentences.zh: 那是……

sentences.en: Turns out, no.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，不会。

sentences.en: Just because you don't have a system doesn't mean that there isn't some built-in, you know, human sense of what is right in the world or what is right for you.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为你没有体系，并不意味着人类内心没有那种关于什么是对的，或者什么对自己是正确的内在感知。

sentences.en: So, um, and it turned out...
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，结果证明……

sentences.en: But there are some rules that you'll break.
sentences.zh: 但有些规则你还是会打破。

sentences.en: Oh, lots.

sentences.en: Absolutely.

sentences.zh: 规则大多是我们自己可以选择的。

sentences.en: And I feel that that's not, like, a burden to navigate.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这并不是一种负担。

sentences.en: I feel like it's a privilege to get to navigate that and to get to play with.
sentences.zh: 我觉得能够去驾驭和玩转这些规则是一种特权。

sentences.en: So, most of the boundaries that we have in the world are, we've all sort of collectively agreed or agreed to not think about them.
sentences.zh: 所以，世界上大多数界限，都是我们集体同意或者同意不去思考的。

sentences.en: We're really good at, I don't know why, we're really good at just being a river that carves a course.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很擅长——我不知道为什么——我们真的很擅长像河流一样开辟河道。

sentences.en: And once we have a deep channel, you just keep flowing in the same channel of thought that you've always flowed in.
sentences.zh: 一旦有了深邃的河道，你就会一直沿着你一直流淌的思维河道流下去。

sentences.en: That's super easy to do.
sentences.zh: 这太容易做到了。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be stuck in the river.
sentences.zh: 我不想被困在河里。

sentences.en: I was like, how do I find the edge and climb up and stick my eyes over the edge of this channel that my mind has carved?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我该如何找到边缘，爬上去，看看我大脑所开辟的这条河道之外的世界？

sentences.en: How do you get out of your own mind in your own space?
sentences.zh: 你如何从自己的思想和空间中走出来？

sentences.en: And the answer to that for me was through generosity.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，答案是通过慷慨。

sentences.en: Okay, tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 好的，跟我说说那个。

sentences.en: I found that I hadn't, I felt really powerless when I was, so for example, when I was leaving my community, I felt really powerless.
sentences.zh: 我发现，我以前——比如当我离开社区时——感到非常无力。

sentences.en: Or at other times in life, I felt, often, felt very powerless.
sentences.zh: 或者在生命中的其他时候，我经常感到非常无力。

sentences.en: And in those times, I found that one of the things that really worked for me was to act with generosity towards things that maybe didn't deserve the generosity.
sentences.zh: 在那些日子里，我发现有一件事对我非常有效，那就是对那些或许并不值得慷慨对待的人或事，依然保持慷慨。

sentences.en: Someone you hate, if you can be generous towards them, or someone who hates you, if you are generous towards them, they have no power over that part of the thing that you control.
sentences.zh: 如果你能对你讨厌的人，或者讨厌你的人保持慷慨，那么在你们的关系中，你所掌控的那部分，他们就无法施加任何影响。

sentences.en: You, weirdly enough, are outside of all of their jurisdiction when you're acting with generosity.
sentences.zh: 说来奇怪，当你以慷慨的态度行事时，你就跳出了他们所有的管辖范围。

sentences.en: You're taking your power back by giving away things.
sentences.zh: 你通过给予，夺回了属于自己的力量。

sentences.en: Yeah, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: Can you give me a concrete example of when you first started to see, like, oh, this is a hack here.
sentences.zh: 你能给我举个具体的例子吗？比如你第一次意识到“哦，这其实是个窍门”的时候。

sentences.en: If I can figure out how to be generous in this interaction or this relationship, what was one of the first things where you gave it that name?
sentences.zh: 如果我能弄清楚如何在这种互动或关系中表现得慷慨，那么你第一次给这种行为命名是什么时候？

sentences.en: Okay, I think I can name an early example.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想我可以举一个早期的例子。

sentences.en: I had a moment in my early 20s where I was with a group of friends, and I was tired of my problems or feeling stuck in my head.
sentences.zh: 我二十出头的时候，有一次和一群朋友在一起，当时我厌倦了自己的问题，或者说感觉陷入了思维的死胡同。

sentences.en: And I found that making a generous surprise for my friends was, I don't know why I initially started doing that, but I think I did that because I was just curious.
sentences.zh: 我发现为朋友准备一份慷慨的惊喜很有用，我不知道最初为什么开始这样做，但我认为是因为我当时很好奇。

sentences.en: I was, like, curious to how they would react.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇他们会有什么反应。

sentences.en: So first it was curiosity.
sentences.zh: 所以起初是出于好奇。

sentences.en: And then my friends experiencing the surprise and me seeing their joy at having something small but generous made for them, like,
sentences.zh: 后来，当朋友们体验到这份惊喜，我看到他们因为收到一份虽小但充满心意的礼物而感到快乐时，

sentences.en: that made me realize that the entire time and process that I'd spent making this little surprise for them, that was all time in which I was, like, really alive.
sentences.zh: 那让我意识到，我花时间为他们准备这份小惊喜的整个过程，在那段时间里，我感觉自己真正地活着。

sentences.en: I think we call that flow state.
sentences.zh: 我想我们称之为“心流状态”。

sentences.en: I wasn't worried about my problems, and I wasn't in any state of fear.
sentences.zh: 我不再担心自己的问题，也没有处于任何恐惧的状态中。

sentences.en: And so there was a moment where the house that my parents built in the wilderness of Alaska, that was only meant to last five years because the end was coming,
sentences.zh: 后来有一次，我父母在阿拉斯加荒野盖的房子，原本只打算住五年，因为当时觉得末日将至，

sentences.en: I started to fall into the swamp.
sentences.zh: 房子开始陷入沼泽。

sentences.en: The foundation rotted because it was just a bunch of stumps.
sentences.zh: 地基腐烂了，因为它只是建在一堆树桩上。

sentences.en: My father built the house.
sentences.zh: 那房子是我父亲盖的。

sentences.en: It was built on a bunch of stumps.
sentences.zh: 它是建在一堆树桩上的。

sentences.en: Well, 25 years later, the stumps were rotting and the house was falling into the swamp.
sentences.zh: 二十五年后，树桩腐烂了，房子开始陷进沼泽里。

sentences.en: And that was a moment where I wasn't on speaking terms with my parents, but I decided that I was, like, you know, here's the thing I can do.
sentences.zh: 那时我和父母正处于冷战期，但我决定，你知道，这是我能做的事。

sentences.en: I can go back and put a foundation under their house.
sentences.zh: 我可以回去给他们的房子打个地基。

sentences.en: And that is an act of generosity that I can do that they won't have any control over how I get to give and what I'm giving.
sentences.zh: 那是一种我能做到的慷慨行为，而他们无法控制我如何给予以及我给予什么。

sentences.en: And that's the only way I know to, like, work on repairing our relationship.
sentences.zh: 这也是我所知道的唯一能修复我们关系的方法。

sentences.en: And so I spent a summer.
sentences.zh: 于是我花了一个夏天。

sentences.en: That was the first time I went back to Alaska, and I spent a summer crawling through the mud under my parents' house, dragging giant beams into the trenches,
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次回到阿拉斯加，我花了一个夏天在父母房子下面的泥地里爬行，把巨大的横梁拖进沟槽里，

sentences.en: jacking the entire house up, and then pouring a cement foundation and setting the house back down on the cement.
sentences.zh: 把整栋房子顶起来，浇筑水泥地基，然后再把房子放回水泥上。

sentences.en: And you're personally rebuilding the foundation of your family home.
sentences.zh: 你是在亲手重建你家庭住宅的地基。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's very on the nose.
sentences.zh: 这真是太直白了。

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of.
sentences.zh: 是啊，算是吧。

sentences.en: Coming up, Indy finds a home in New York City, and he tells me about a current project he's working on.
sentences.zh: 接下来，Indy 在纽约市找到了归属感，他跟我聊起了他目前正在进行的一个项目。

sentences.en: It's one that has sparked a lot of conversations for me around the dinner table.
sentences.zh: 这个项目在我的餐桌上引发了很多讨论。

sentences.en: How would you feel if you found out that your friends were paying for someone to secretly create good luck for you for six years?
sentences.zh: 如果你发现你的朋友们雇人暗中为你创造了六年的好运，你会作何感想？

sentences.en: Yeah, we had a lot of long conversations about what the ethical boundary was.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们关于道德界限在哪里进行了很多长时间的讨论。

sentences.en: Indy Austin moved to New York City in his late 20s.
sentences.zh: Indy Austin 在二十多岁末期搬到了纽约市。

sentences.en: He said he was immediately attracted to the energy and also to the sense that there were places to uncover and to infiltrate boundaries to be played with.
sentences.zh: 他说他立刻被这里的活力所吸引，也因为这里有许多地方可以去探索，有许多界限可以去渗透和挑战。

sentences.en: I'd never been to a place where I was like, oh, there's space here to make something.
sentences.zh: 我从未去过一个让我觉得“哦，这里有空间可以创造点什么”的地方。

sentences.en: I think part of the exploring what this place is as a foreigner to the city definitely is just physically moving around through the city.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一名外来者，探索这个城市的一部分，绝对就是通过身体力行地在城市中穿梭。

sentences.en: But part of it is exploring what people's norms and rules are.
sentences.zh: 但探索的一部分也在于了解人们的规范和规则是什么。

sentences.en: And it's very interesting to see who cares about what.
sentences.zh: 观察谁在意什么，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And so on some streets, it doesn't matter what buildings are on the street, there's like an eagle-eyed old lady sitting in the window, right?
sentences.zh: 在某些街道上，不管街上有什么建筑，总会有一位目光敏锐的老太太坐在窗边，对吧？

sentences.en: You know it.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: And she knows everything that's going on in the street, and there's nothing like she is watching.
sentences.zh: 她知道街上发生的一切，没有什么能逃过她的眼睛。

sentences.en: Other streets, though, no one's watching and no one cares.
sentences.zh: 但在其他街道，没人关注，也没人在意。

sentences.en: So I'd be like, why?
sentences.zh: 所以我常想，为什么？

sentences.en: And I couldn't always tell why.
sentences.zh: 我并不总能看出原因。

sentences.en: It wasn't obvious to me why one should be in one place versus the other.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，为什么一个地方应该这样而另一个地方应该那样，并不显而易见。

sentences.en: So, number one, I was just like, who cares about what?
sentences.zh: 所以，第一，我只是在想，谁在意什么？

sentences.en: And the moment you start asking yourself who cares about what, you start seeing all the cracks and the gaps.
sentences.zh: 当你开始问自己谁在意什么时，你就会开始看到所有的裂缝和缺口。

sentences.en: And there are cracks in the care all over the city.
sentences.zh: 整个城市到处都是这种“关注的裂缝”。

sentences.en: And when you go into those cracks, that's where you find space to make transformation happen
sentences.zh: 当你进入这些裂缝时，你就会发现创造变革的空间，

sentences.en: or space to bring some love and attention.
sentences.zh: 或者带来爱与关注的空间。

sentences.en: And that love and attention is really transformative and really powerful.
sentences.zh: 而那种爱与关注是非常具有变革性且强大的。

sentences.en: Do you remember the first experience that somebody offered to compensate you for that you did?
sentences.zh: 你还记得有人第一次提出为你提供的服务付费是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: No one's ever asked me this question.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人问过我这个问题。

sentences.en: And I think it was this guy who came to a friend's birthday party where I had done a tiny little photo scavenger hunt thing,
sentences.zh: 我想是一个参加朋友生日派对的人，当时我搞了一个小型的照片寻宝游戏，

sentences.en: a little miniature version of these scavenger hunts that we would do.
sentences.zh: 就是我们常玩的那种寻宝游戏的微缩版。

sentences.en: We'd get a bunch of friends together, and we'd do these photo scavenger hunts where everyone gets a little disposable camera
sentences.zh: 我们会召集一群朋友，进行这种照片寻宝游戏，每个人都会拿到一台一次性相机，

sentences.en: and ten captions to photos that don't exist yet.
sentences.zh: 以及十个还没拍出来的照片的标题。

sentences.en: And then we'd send them out into the city, and then I'll congregate back at somebody's apartment and go through all the photos.
sentences.zh: 然后我们把他们派到城市里，最后在某个人的公寓集合，查看所有的照片。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, how fun.
sentences.zh: 天哪，太有趣了。

sentences.en: So, like, an example would be, a caption would be like, look how many fit in here.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，一个标题可能是“看看这里能挤下多少人”。

sentences.en: Something like that.
sentences.zh: 类似这样的。

sentences.en: And this guy came to one of these things, just a fun thing we're doing for friends.
sentences.zh: 有个家伙参加了其中一次活动，那只是我们为朋友举办的娱乐活动。

sentences.en: And he was like, can you do, like, a birthday party?
sentences.zh: 他问我，你能办个生日派对吗？

sentences.en: And I said, no, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我想不行。

sentences.en: So, I said, no, I'd love to hire you to do this birthday party.
sentences.zh: 于是我说，不，我想雇你来办这个生日派对。

sentences.en: I said, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我说，我想不行。

sentences.en: But maybe there is something you need that I could make.
sentences.zh: 但也许你有什么需要我制作的东西。

sentences.en: And then we talked about it, and it ended up that what he really wanted wasn't a big birthday party.
sentences.zh: 后来我们谈了谈，结果他真正想要的并不是一个大型生日派对。

sentences.en: He really wanted to do something special for his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 他真正想为他的女朋友做点特别的事情。

sentences.en: And I was like, I can help you make a really good gift.
sentences.zh: 我说，我可以帮你准备一份非常棒的礼物。

sentences.en: But that process, I didn't know I was doing a design process.
sentences.zh: 但那个过程，我当时并不知道自己在进行设计流程。

sentences.en: I was just having a talk to figure out what the thing was.
sentences.zh: 我只是在交谈，弄清楚那到底是什么东西。

sentences.en: But that actually turned out to be what a design process is, where you spend time with someone to actually learn what they really need, or where they wish to end up,
sentences.zh: 但那实际上就是设计流程的样子，你花时间和某人在一起，真正了解他们到底需要什么，或者他们希望达到什么结果，

sentences.en: or how they want the people to feel when they're done.
sentences.zh: 或者他们希望人们在结束后有什么样的感受。

sentences.en: And usually people can answer those questions.
sentences.zh: 通常人们能回答这些问题。

sentences.en: Usually people know, oh, I want my people to feel this kind of way, or I hope.
sentences.zh: 通常人们知道，哦，我希望我的人有这种感觉，或者我希望。

sentences.en: My hope is this kind of feeling.
sentences.zh: 我的愿望是这种感觉。

sentences.en: And almost always, you can engineer a path towards that state.
sentences.zh: 几乎总是，你可以设计一条通往那种状态的路径。

sentences.en: I live in the Bay Area, and I hear the word design a lot around.
sentences.zh: 我住在湾区，经常听到“设计”这个词。

sentences.en: Can we find a better one?
sentences.zh: 我们能找到一个更好的词吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think the thing that I'm sort of struck by after hearing you talk is, as a designer, like you are, how different the manifestation of what you design, what it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听了你的话，我感到震撼的是，作为一名设计师，你所设计的东西的呈现方式是多么不同。

sentences.en: Because you have generosity at the core, instead of designing for clicks, or growth, or, and so it makes me curious just how you,
sentences.zh: 因为你的核心是慷慨，而不是为了点击率或增长而设计，这让我很好奇，当你……

sentences.en: when you're around like tech people who talk about design, and I imagine you think about design thinking, and a lot of that comes out of the tech world.
sentences.zh: 当你和那些谈论设计的科技界人士在一起时，我想你一定思考过“设计思维”，而那很多源自科技界。

sentences.en: Are they people with whom you feel camaraderie?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们是志同道合的人吗？

sentences.en: Do you feel like you're on the other side of the fence from them, because you don't share sort of fundamental values?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得因为你们的基本价值观不同，你站在了他们的对立面？

sentences.en: How do you feel?
sentences.zh: 你感觉如何？

sentences.en: Oh, I am fundamentally part of the resistance.
sentences.zh: 哦，我从根本上就是抵抗者的一员。

sentences.en: You are?
sentences.zh: 你是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you feel like you're studying their tools to, like, be part of the resistance?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你在研究他们的工具，为了成为抵抗者的一部分吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No, their tools are not very useful.
sentences.zh: 不，他们的工具没什么用。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: No, their tools are about getting.
sentences.zh: 不，他们的工具是为了“获取”。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm not Amish.
sentences.zh: 我不是阿米什人。

sentences.en: I use a phone when I need to, or I'll use tech as necessary, but there's very little of use to learn about tools that are attempting to get, I think, for me.
sentences.zh: 我需要时会用手机，或者在必要时使用科技，但对我来说，学习那些试图“获取”的工具几乎没什么用。

sentences.en: I almost never feel inspired by tools that are designed to capture your attention, to take something from you, to convince you of something.
sentences.zh: 我几乎从不被那些旨在捕获你注意力、从你身上索取东西、试图说服你的工具所激励。

sentences.en: I grew up with weapons-grade attention-capturing tools, and so most of the tech stuff doesn't resonate for me.
sentences.zh: 我是在武器级的注意力捕获工具中长大的，所以大多数科技产品对我来说没什么共鸣。

sentences.en: If it had any generosity at its core, or any connection to beauty, maybe there'd be something there.
sentences.zh: 如果它们的核心有任何慷慨，或者与美有任何联系，也许还有点意思。

sentences.en: But most of the tech stuff that comes out of the Bay Area is remarkably uninterested in beauty, and remarkably uninterested in creating something generous in the world.
sentences.zh: 但大多数来自湾区的科技产品对美毫无兴趣，对在世界上创造慷慨的东西也毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: Did you have to figure out, this is a crass question, but I'm just curious, having done it as a way of caring for your community, or the way that you socialized,
sentences.zh: 你是否必须弄清楚——这是一个粗鲁的问题，但我只是好奇——当你把它作为一种关怀社区的方式，或者你社交的方式，

sentences.en: and then it becomes something that you're selling, how did you figure out your rate?
sentences.zh: 然后它变成了你出售的东西，你是如何确定你的费率的？

sentences.en: Number one, I'm not selling the thing.
sentences.zh: 第一，我不是在兜售这个东西。

sentences.en: People are coming to me and asking me to do something for them, so I'm not like...
sentences.zh: 人们来找我，请求我为他们做点什么，所以我不是在……

sentences.en: You're not out hustling.
sentences.zh: 你不是在四处奔波揽活。

sentences.en: Or it doesn't, the hustle's very different, it doesn't work like that.
sentences.zh: 或者说，那种奔波非常不同，不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: I'm not specifically attempting to get a lot of new clients.
sentences.zh: 我并没有刻意试图获取大量新客户。

sentences.en: I'm trying to make work for the people that I can really make a difference for, and that isn't everybody, and it shouldn't be.
sentences.zh: 我试图为那些我能真正产生影响的人创作作品，那并不是每个人，也不应该是每个人。

sentences.en: I once gave someone, I once told someone that I thought what they really needed was to go on a cruise, take a Disney cruise.
sentences.zh: 我曾经告诉过某人，我认为他们真正需要的是去度假，去坐迪士尼游轮。

sentences.en: And it was, I think it was true.
sentences.zh: 我想那是真的。

sentences.en: It was truly what I actually...
sentences.zh: 那确实是我真正……

sentences.en: Designed by a designed experience.
sentences.zh: 由设计出来的体验。

sentences.en: I thought, this is actually what you should do.
sentences.zh: 我想，这才是你真正应该做的。

sentences.en: They were like, no, but what, shouldn't, what?
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，但是什么，不应该，什么？

sentences.en: Are I supposed to want the artisanal bespoke thing?
sentences.zh: 难道我不该想要那种手工定制的东西吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, I don't know, I think actually you'll get everything you need from that cruise.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，我不知道，我想其实你从那次游轮旅行中就能得到你需要的一切。

sentences.en: They had a great time on the cruise.
sentences.zh: 他们在游轮上玩得很开心。

sentences.en: Do you, when you are approached by paying clients, like, how much work do you say no to?
sentences.zh: 当有付费客户找上门时，你会拒绝多少工作？

sentences.en: And is there a pattern to what you say?
sentences.zh: 你拒绝的理由有什么规律吗？

sentences.en: Like, I don't need to do that.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不需要做那个。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any real pattern, but I have some personal formulas or something, or like criteria, which is not always necessary, but I have them if I need them.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有什么真正的规律，但我有一些个人的公式或标准，虽然不一定总是必要，但如果需要，我有这些标准。

sentences.en: So sometimes someone comes to me and they want something, and it's not clear to me if it's something I can contribute to or not, or I don't know what the path in is yet.
sentences.zh: 所以有时有人来找我，他们想要点什么，我不确定我是否能贡献什么，或者我还没找到切入点。

sentences.en: And so then I start asking myself some questions, or I can ask them some questions.
sentences.zh: 于是我就开始问自己一些问题，或者我可以问他们一些问题。

sentences.en: So, for example, I know, just off the bat, that I'm very motivated by generosity.
sentences.zh: 例如，我直接就知道，我非常受慷慨精神的驱动。

sentences.en: I love place.
sentences.zh: 我热爱“地方感”。

sentences.en: So things that arise out of place are really potent.
sentences.zh: 所以从特定地点衍生出来的事物非常有力量。

sentences.en: Intimacy is very important to me, and I love making intimate experiences, even if they're large scale.
sentences.zh: 亲密感对我来说非常重要，我喜欢创造亲密的体验，即使是大型活动。

sentences.en: So sometimes we make something for thousands of people, but there'll be real intimate moments in it.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我们为成千上万的人制作东西，但其中会有真正亲密的时刻。

sentences.en: And, of course, transgression.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有“越界”。

sentences.en: Transgression.
sentences.zh: 越界。

sentences.en: If people are willing to transgress, it doesn't have to mean physically.
sentences.zh: 如果人们愿意越界，并不一定非得是身体上的。

sentences.en: I think trespassing is really easy to point to because it's very photogenic.
sentences.zh: 我认为“擅闯”很容易指出来，因为它非常上镜。

sentences.en: More complicated to talk about is other kinds of transgression.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是谈论其他形式的越界。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Emotional transgression, or perhaps consent transgression.
sentences.zh: 情感上的越界，或者可能是关于同意的越界。

sentences.en: An experience Indy is working on now plays with consent.
sentences.zh: Indy 目前正在进行的一个体验项目就涉及了“同意”这一概念。

sentences.en: In 2019, he was approached by a group of friends.
sentences.zh: 2019年，一群朋友找到了他。

sentences.en: This woman came to me and said,
sentences.zh: 这个女人来找我说，

sentences.en: I've got a friend who is really depressed, and she has really terrible luck.
sentences.zh: 我有个朋友非常抑郁，而且她运气特别差。

sentences.en: Is she depressed because she has terrible luck, or does she have terrible luck because she's always depressed?
sentences.zh: 她是抑郁了才运气差，还是因为运气差才一直抑郁？

sentences.en: Well, chicken egg.
sentences.zh: 嗯，先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题。

sentences.en: They asked Indy to make their friend a party.
sentences.zh: 他们请Indy为他们的朋友办一场派对。

sentences.en: It seems like the first experience people usually ask for,
sentences.zh: 这似乎是人们通常最先要求的体验，

sentences.en: and the one Indy says no to the most frequently, is a party.
sentences.zh: 也是Indy拒绝得最频繁的一项，就是办派对。

sentences.en: Indy thought about it and proposed something different,
sentences.zh: Indy思考了一下，提出了不同的方案，

sentences.en: to focus on changing how their friend perceived her life.
sentences.zh: 重点在于改变她朋友对生活的看法。

sentences.en: I think the way to do this is long-term.
sentences.zh: 我认为实现这一目标的方式是长期的。

sentences.en: So if we made some luck occur in her life,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们让她的生活中发生一些好运，

sentences.en: in some respect it feels to me like luck is actually just pretty mechanical and procedural.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我觉得运气实际上是非常机械和程序化的。

sentences.en: And for example, like if you had an uncle who like had some good connections to the thing,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你有个叔叔，他刚好在某件事上有很好的门路，

sentences.en: and your uncle was just like,
sentences.zh: 然后你叔叔就说，

sentences.en: hey, I got you hooked up with the thing, the tickets to the thing.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我帮你搞定了那件事，搞到了那件事的票。

sentences.en: You'd be like, wow, I'm so lucky.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，哇，我真是太幸运了。

sentences.en: But like, no one else has got that uncle.
sentences.zh: 但其实，没人有那样的叔叔。

sentences.en: You just happen to have the uncle.
sentences.zh: 你只是刚好有那个叔叔而已。

sentences.en: Wow, that's great.
sentences.zh: 哇，那太棒了。

sentences.en: But that's like some coincidence you can't control.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一种你无法控制的巧合。

sentences.en: But maybe I could pretend to be the uncle for this person,
sentences.zh: 但也许我可以假装成那个人的叔叔，

sentences.en: and hook him up with some stuff.
sentences.zh: 帮他搞定一些事情。

sentences.en: And maybe it would have that sensation of feeling like you're really fortunate.
sentences.zh: 也许这会带来一种你真的很幸运的感觉。

sentences.en: Things are going your way.
sentences.zh: 一切都如你所愿。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm only guessing.
sentences.zh: 我只是在猜测。

sentences.en: But I said, if you will commit to funding this for six years,
sentences.zh: 但我说，如果你愿意承诺资助这件事六年，

sentences.en: I'll commit to doing it.
sentences.zh: 我就承诺去执行它。

sentences.en: And what we'll do is we'll make serendipity, good luck, happen in the life of your friend.
sentences.zh: 我们要做的就是让机缘巧合，也就是好运，在你的朋友生活中发生。

sentences.en: But you can't tell her that you're doing this to her.
sentences.zh: 但你不能告诉她你在对她做这些事。

sentences.en: Until year six, you have to decide.
sentences.zh: 直到第六年，你才需要做决定。

sentences.en: And then you have to decide whether you tell her or don't tell her and how.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须决定是否要告诉她，以及如何告诉她。

sentences.en: So, and then the very first thing, the very first thing we did,
